domain: Evidence adjudication for multi-round review ledgers — claim-status discipline (raw / verified / refuted / bounded), independent confirmation versus lens self-attestation, citation forensics against source code, tracking of claims that silently depend on already-refuted claims, and the equivalence/clustering predicates that decide whether two filed contracts are one candidate or two.
axioms: A file:line citation written by the lens that filed the claim is a claim, not a confirmation; verification requires a check performed by a party that did not benefit from the finding.

Disposition is not binary — 'verified', 'refuted', and 'bounded to a narrower scope' are different outcomes, and a charter that offers only the first two forces overclaiming on partially-true findings.

A candidate inherits the status of the premises its contract rests on; if a supporting finding was refuted or repaired, that dependency must travel with the candidate into ranking or the ranking is built on a knocked-down premise.
Clustering happens before scoring and therefore decides outcomes: an incomplete equivalence key silently merges distinct candidates or splits one, and no downstream comparison can recover from it.
'Give X its strongest contract or explain why it dissolves' is only executable if the dissolution test is named; otherwise the answer is decided by whichever framing is written first.
Unverified findings may inform prioritization but must not be cited as settled in a recommendation; the charter is defective if it permits that laundering rather than merely failing to forbid it.
primitives: finding id and its status field (raw / verified / refuted / demoted-to-convergence)
self-attestation versus independent adjudication as distinct evidence classes
citation triple: claim, file:line, and the check that would falsify it
refutation-dependency edge (candidate → refuted or repaired parent finding)
disposition vocabulary and the artifact each disposition must name
equivalence/clustering key and its known-missing dimensions (spend, issuing authority, persistence)
dissolution test for a candidate absorbed into an existing phase or contract
coupling rule between disposition status and eligibility for shortlisting
failure_mode: Procedural bias — will judge whether a conclusion is properly established and can pass a well-documented but substantively wrong disposition while flagging a correct one that is under-cited.
Cannot assess whether a candidate is a good design; it has no criteria for semantic distinctness, taste, or cost, so it under-serves the ranking half of the charter entirely.
Tends to inflate process requirements — can demand verification machinery whose cost exceeds the decision's stakes, especially for P3-shaped findings that will never be load-bearing.
Blind to measurement feasibility: will accept 'verify against the runtime' as executable without asking whether the runtime exposes the quantity at all.
Prone to treating the prior ledger as authoritative structure rather than as one more artifact that may itself be mis-clustered.
Weak on aggregate effects — audits findings one at a time and can miss that a set of individually adequate dispositions still leaves the frontier's top unverified.
